height.note: sampling is world-subdiv. raw is normalized (heightUnit normalized): metres from the world height map, mapped so sea level (0 m) is units.seaLevel. It is a Catmull-Rom read of WorldData.heightM plus world-anchored detail, not a bilinear of stored WorldData.heights. Samples are every 2 m. Sample [0] is originInner in absolute inner-tile metres, and originCorner equals originInner. The lattice covers the expanded grid plus one subdiv sample of apron on each side. v0.6 controller: Catmull-Rom across the lattice, then y = clamp((raw - minRaw) / (maxRaw - minRaw), 0, 1) * reliefMeters. minRaw/maxRaw are the percentile clip from 0.02 to 0.98, widened so the span is at least 0.12, then padded by 5% of that span on each side, so a small continental delta does not become a full reliefMeters cliff. detailMeters (0.4) is the legacy micro-relief hint and is not baked into raw. v0.7 detail is baked into layers.heightM and seeded by units.detailSeed. Water stays flat at layers.water.level for a v0.6 reader. A settlement pad lifts building lots, roads, zones, the spawn, and the respawn anchor to at least 0.6 m above sea level and blends back to the sampled terrain. Cells that stay below sea level are tagged water.

heightM.note: World metres above sea level (units.seaLevelM = 0, units.heightDatum = sea). Same lattice as layers.height: subdivMeters, originInner, w, h. enc is b64i16le, little-endian int16, metres = int16 * quantM. quantM is 0.2 because int16 decimetres only reach ±3,276.8 m and trench floors are about −4,000 m. Each sample is a Catmull-Rom read of WorldData.heightM (one value per 8 m world tile) plus detail noise. The detail seed is units.detailSeed, mixed with absolute world coordinates, not the area id. Two areas that cover the same point encode the same metres, apart from a settlement pad that only lifts the area that owns the lots, roads, and zones. The pad is included: those features sit at least 0.6 m above sea. Controller playable height is sampleMetres * units.verticalExaggeration. verticalExaggeration is one world constant (a gentle compression of true metres). Apply that same factor in every area. Do not refit min/max per area. layers.height.raw and reliefMeters stay for v0.6 readers. They are not the metre heights.

water.note: No water cells in the playable mask. level is still the normalized sea level (0.36, which is 0 m) remapped with height.minRaw and height.maxRaw so a v0.6 controller has a water line.

notes: Street chunks are regenerated in (y, x) order for two passes. Edges do not depend on which neighbour the session generated first.
Spawn is the road or dirt cell nearest the place centroid, otherwise the nearest walkable cell. The live walker is not baked in, so the same seed and place hash the same.

reliefMeters is 15 times the highest per-biome multiplier among the place biome and its world tiles. Hills use 2 and mountains use 3, so they rise above the 15 m base. This is not the continental elevationMeters scale.
Water level is derived. See layers.water.note. world-map does not store a water line or depth.

roads.polylines are centerlines on the 3 m grid (north-west corner of each road cell). rank, widthM, and surface match layers.surface. roads.worldTiles stay the coarse WorldData.paths flags and are not filled from polylines. Overworld paths are stamped between cities and towns, so a village can have local polylines and an empty worldTiles list. Ground classes road and dirt remain the v0.5 road mask.

The border ring is visual only. Walkable cells are grid.mask (1 = place tile). grid.borderMask uses the same encoding (1 = ring cell with world terrain, 0 = void or playable) and is not walkable. The controller should use Catmull-Rom on layers.height.

The ring copies the world-tile biome and a simplified ground (grass, sand, rock, dirt, water, and road along world paths). It has no buildings and no props. Neighbour names stay metadata. Void cells are 0 in both masks; ignore their biome and ground bytes.
Desert maps to ground class sand. Mountain maps to rock. Other dry land is grass unless a path, lot, plaza, or yard overrides it. Snow stays grass.

v0.2 buildings add a human-scale structure inside a larger plot. footW/footD are the structure AABB. tiles is the world-aligned mask (yard, floor, wall, door, window, tower). rotation is 0, 90, 180, or 270. door and doorCell are the opening after that rotation.
Season is the tileset row for the place biome (summer, autumn, winter, lush), not a simulated calendar.
meta.exportedAt, meta.timeOfDayHours, npcs, and session are excluded from meta.hash.

population is the town census for a city, town, village, or hamlet, and it is part of meta.hash. count = round(avg × (the dwelling count when mode is perHouse, otherwise 1) × a seeded ±25% jitter from the world seed and place id). The jitter does not use the sim RNG. named is the count of named residents (real map entities) for this place, so crowd = max(0, count − named) does not depend on npcs. homes lists dwelling building indexes, repeated once per 30 m² of structure. hotspots are the plaza centre, market stands, tavern doors, and wells in area metres (offset from innerOrigin, y down). The named residents are not part of the crowd. A missing population field means there is no crowd; v0.4 readers ignore the field.

v0.6 is additive. buildings[].type stays the legacy sprite (shop, tavern, cottage-1, …). specialty is the §5 id and kit is the manifest name. layers.biome id 7 is Badlands; legendAliases.Heath is Badlands for one version. Ids 15–26 are reserved names and are not emitted yet. layers.surface, area.settlement, zones, segments, minigameSlots, and meta.kitVersion are new. A camp, hamlet, village, town, or city writes area.settlement with variant default. City layout is the town row until the city tier is built. minigameSlots are deterministic and part of the hash. Schedules are hours. peeloff is set on wild slots and ford_crossing.

v0.7 is additive. layers.height.raw, minRaw, maxRaw, and reliefMeters are unchanged in meaning: a v0.6 reader still remaps raw into reliefMeters and compares raw with units.seaLevel. layers.heightM is the same lattice in world metres (sea level 0). units.seaLevelM is 0, units.heightDatum is sea, units.verticalExaggeration is the single playable scale (apply it to heightM; do not refit per area), and units.detailSeed is the world-anchored detail seed. Playable height is heightM times verticalExaggeration.

v0.8 is additive. population.crowd is { profile: "trailbound", seed, mix, culture: null, tier } on a city, town, village, or hamlet. mix rows are { role, w } in role order. w is a multiple of 0.001 and the thousandths sum to 1000. Roles are farmer, merchant, smith, guard, sailor, fisher, noble, pioneer, laborer, crafter. Nobles are omitted below town. Sailor and fisher are omitted unless the place has open water, a Sand coast, a Marsh river, or a dock, quay, wharf, harbour, pier, or port building. crowd.seed is FNV-1a 32 of utf8("crowd"), 0, little-endian uint32 world seed, 0, utf8(place id), then xor-folded (h ^ h>>>16), or 1 when that fold is 0. It does not use the sim RNG. Crowd member i (from 0) is the same FNV-1a of little-endian crowd.seed then little-endian i, xor-folded the same way. The census formula is unchanged. A grove or camp still omits population. Older readers ignore crowd.
